Synopsis:
Discussion between Gimbleboc and Taman before the scene against them triggers. They're arguing about whether to investigate the crash (this segues into the beginning of their intertactive dialogue when you get near enough)

Cluster Contexts:
- CHA_Outside_BanditWestInteraction.json: Alternate version of the confrontation scene between Gimblebock and his bandits at the crypt - triggers if the player approaches the scene from the side, alerting Warryn first.
- CHA_Outside_BanditInteraction.json: The bandits are encountered near an abandoned chapel and are in the middle of an argument among themselves about whether or not to investigate (and loot) the crashed nautoloid (a spaceship) when the player approaches them. The player can convince them to clear off via lies or threats, or else is forced to fight them. A gnome named Gimblebock is in charge of this group, with his underlings, Quelanna and/or Taman, chiming in at points with their concerns.
- CHA_Outside_Bandit_Melee_01_Dead.json: Speak with Dead dialogue with Gimblebock - the leader of the bandits who're looting the ruined chapel near where the player first wakes up. Gimblebock's answers are fragmented, cryptic. He can only draw on info that he knew when he was alive, and will refuse to speak to his killer if he recognises them. After a maximum of five questions, he'll fall silent for good.
- WYR_NGB_Ironhand_Trespass.json: Trespass dialog started if player enters Ironhand gnomes hideout in WYR before helping gnomes in the Checkpoint Scene.
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_KoboldLooter.json: Automatically initiated dialogue after players bash/prise open a coffin with Bugthimble, a tetchy and mistrustful Kobold, just trying to live her best life looting the coffin and the nasty adventurers dug her upt! She wears a face covering helmet.Players have either dug here expecting to find "Enough valuables to settle matters between us" as the note they found said (Tough letter, found on the Courier by Scratch) or just decided to dig up a grave for fun.

- Taman: Why don't we just wait a while? Make sure it's safe. || [context] NodeContext: Cautious, defensive (node 4)

Sample 2:
- Gimblebock: Either we act now, or someone else will pick that wreck clean and leave us nothing. || [context] NodeContext: Short-tempered (node 3)

Sample 3:
- Gimblebock: There could be all sorts of loot in that thing - don't you want to be rich? || [context] NodeContext: Short-tempered (node 6)
- Taman: Of course I want to be rich - but not if it'll get me killed. || [context] NodeContext: Cautious, defensive (node 0)

context: A small band of looters led by the short‑tempered gnome Gimblebock is camped by an abandoned chapel beside a crashed nautiloid, and he and his cautious underling Taman are arguing over whether to risk investigating the wreck for treasure. Their bickering — Gimblebock pushing for quick action and Taman warning of danger — plays out just before the interactive scene begins when the player approaches. The player’s approach can change how the confrontation unfolds (you can scare or lie them off, or be forced into combat), and an alternate version of the encounter can trigger if the party is approached from the side and different NPCs (like Warryn) are alerted.
